settings.label: API key
settings.meaning: Reaches the account's audiences with full access to the account. Keep it on the server, never in a browser or a mobile app. Its suffix after the dash (us6) is the account's data center.
settings.whereToFind: Profile › Extras › API keys › Create A Key. It's shown once, and it can stop working (its user leaves the account, or it expires): plan to rotate it. Mailchimp has no test mode: use a separate audience for test.

settings.label: Server prefix
settings.meaning: The account's data center, the first part of the API's host (us6 in us6.api.mailchimp.com). Read from the API key when unset.
settings.whereToFind: The API key's suffix after the dash, or the first part of the address of the Mailchimp app (us6.admin.mailchimp.com). Leave it unset.

settings.label: Audience ID
settings.meaning: The audience (list) the app's contacts are kept in.
settings.whereToFind: Audience › All contacts › Settings › Audience name and defaults: Audience ID. Use a separate audience for test.

settings.label: Webhook signing secret
settings.meaning: Checks that a webhook came from Mailchimp. Mailchimp makes it when the webhook is created and shows it once.
settings.whereToFind: Audience › Settings › Webhooks › Create New Webhook shows it after Save; webhooks.create returns it as signingSecret. Lost, it can't be read again: delete the webhook and create it again.

operations.name: members.upsert
operations.purpose: Adds a contact to the audience or updates it, by the MD5 of the lowercased email; status_if_new is the status a new contact gets.

operations.name: members.get
operations.purpose: Reads one contact, whatever its status: subscribed, pending, unsubscribed, cleaned or archived.

operations.name: members.update
operations.purpose: Changes a contact's merge fields, status, language or email address.

operations.name: members.archive
operations.purpose: Archives a contact: it stays in the account's history but is no longer in the audience, and it can be added again.

operations.name: members.deletePermanently
operations.purpose: Deletes everything personal about a contact and removes it from the audience. The address can never be added through the API again: only the person can re-subscribe, through a Mailchimp form.

operations.name: members.updateTags
operations.purpose: Adds tags to a contact (status active) and removes them (inactive). A tag that doesn't exist is created.

operations.name: members.batch
operations.purpose: Adds or updates up to 500 contacts in one call; update_existing says whether existing contacts' status changes. Answers with the ones created, the ones updated and the ones that failed.

operations.name: mergeFields.list
operations.purpose: Lists the audience's merge fields: each one's tag (FNAME), name, type and whether it's required.

operations.name: webhooks.create
operations.purpose: Creates a webhook on the audience for the events and sources chosen. The answer carries the signing secret, once.

operations.name: webhooks.delete
operations.purpose: Deletes one of the audience's webhooks.

signature.description: The header is t=<Unix seconds>,v1=<hex>, where v1 is the HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the webhook's signing secret, of the timestamp, a period and the raw request body ("<t>.<body>"), compared in constant time. Deliveries whose timestamp is more than five minutes from now are refused. The body is application/x-www-form-urlencoded with bracketed keys (type=unsubscribe&data[email]=…), and is verified before it's decoded. Mailchimp checks the URL with a GET when the webhook is created, which is answered 200.

events.meaning: A contact subscribed to the audience.
A contact unsubscribed, or was unsubscribed by an admin.
A contact's profile (merge fields, interests) changed.
A contact's email address changed: data has the old and the new.
Mailchimp cleaned an address from the audience because mail to it bounced.
A campaign to the audience was sent or cancelled.
